title: From Bits to Qubits: The Theory and Practice of Quantum Data Encoding
authors: Xiao-Ming Zhang, Arthur G. Rattew, Bujiao Wu, Georgios Styliaris, Xiaoming Sun, Bálint Koczor, Xiao Yuan
abstract: Encoding classical data into quantum systems is a foundational step in the execution of nearly all quantum algorithms, and a critical bottleneck in realizing practical quantum advantage. This review provides a comprehensive account of the concepts, algorithms, and practical considerations associated with quantum data encoding. We trace the development from its early conceptual foundations to recent advances, considering commonly used access models, such as quantum state preparation, unitary synthesis, QRAM and block encoding. We survey the circuit size, depth, space-time tradeoffs, as well as non-Clifford resources required for fault-tolerant implementation. We also discuss the roles of different access models in quantum algorithms. Special attention is given to structured data, such as sparse data, Boolean functions and data represented by tensor networks. This review bridges theory and applications, serving both as a pedagogical guide for newcomers and as a reference for active researchers. We also highlight the pivotal role of quantum data encoding in quantum computing and provide insights into future directions that will enable quantum advantage.
summary: This review systematically surveys the theory and practice of quantum data encoding, which is essential for running quantum algorithms. It details multiple encoding methods—such as state preparation, QRAM, and block encoding—and analyzes their associated resource costs like circuit depth and size. The work serves as a vital guide for both newcomers and experts in quantum computing hardware and algorithm design.
main_problem: Encoding classical data (like vectors or matrices) into quantum states or circuits is a fundamental and critical bottleneck for achieving practical quantum advantage.
main_result: The review provides a comprehensive survey of various encoding techniques, including quantum state preparation, QRAM utilization, and block encoding, detailing their respective circuit complexities.
method: The paper surveys theoretical concepts and algorithms, analyzing resource costs (circuit size, depth, T-count) associated with different data loading models.
model_or_system: The analysis is based on the standard qubit-based circuit model, focusing on encoding classical information into quantum states or unitary operations.
key_observables: Circuit size, circuit depth, T-count, and the fidelity of the resulting quantum state.
important_parameters: The complexity scales with the size of the classical data (e.g., vector length N or matrix dimension).
main_assumptions: It assumes classical data are deterministic and fully known in advance, and it is limited to the standard qubit model.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the conceptual flow from classical bits to quantum qubits via various encoding processes like state preparation and block encoding.
paper_structure: The paper is structured as a comprehensive review, systematically covering quantum state preparation, unitary synthesis, QRAM implementations, structured data encoding (sparse data, Boolean functions), and block-encoding generalizations.
why_interesting: It provides a crucial theoretical roadmap for researchers aiming to implement quantum algorithms, especially those involving complex data structures or simulation inputs, by quantifying the required quantum resources.
